title: Arbitrary base change for qcqs etale compact support
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring. Work in the bounded-below derived categories of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For any separated finite-type morphism $h:T\to B$ of quasi-compact and quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], a compactification $c=(j:T\hookrightarrow\overline T,p:\overline T\to B)$ consists of a quasi-compact open immersion $j$ and a proper morphism $p$ with $h=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification]; write $Rh_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be such a morphism, let $g:Y'\to Y$ be any morphism with $Y'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and form $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a compactification $c$ of $f$, let $c'$ be its base change to $Y'$. Then for every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ there is a natural isomorphism $g^{-1}Rf_!^cK\cong Rf'_!^{c'}g'^{-1}K$, where inverse image of constant-coefficient module sheaves is applied termwise [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image].

proof.text: Write $\overline X'=\overline X\times_Y Y'$ and let $\overline g:\overline X'\to\overline X$ be the projection. The inverse image $W=\overline g^{-1}(j(X))$, equipped with the restricted structure sheaf, is an open subscheme of $\overline X'$ by [def-weil-open-immersion]. A morphism $a:S\to\overline X'$ factors uniquely through $W$ exactly when $\overline g a$ factors through $j:X\to\overline X$: both factorizations are the restriction of the map of locally ringed spaces to that open. Thus $W$ represents $X\times_{\overline X}\overline X'$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], maps to this fibre product are precisely pairs of maps to $X$ and $Y'$ whose composites to $Y$ agree, so it is canonically $X'=X\times_Y Y'$. This gives an open immersion $j':X'\to\overline X'$, the two cartesian squares with vertical maps $(j,j')$ and $(p,p')$, and $f'=p'j'$. Properness of $p'$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](b), and quasi-compactness of $j'$ from [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). Part (1) of the latter node makes $g:Y'\to Y$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, since $Y,Y'$ are qcqs; part (3) then makes its base change $g':X'\to X$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and part (2), with qcqs target $X$, makes $X'$ qcqs. The separated finite-type hypothesis for $f'$ follows from [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Consequently $c'=(j',p')$ is a compactification in exactly the sense of [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification].

proof.text: The finite additive sequence $0,1,2\cdot1,\ldots$ in $\Lambda$ repeats, so there is $N>0$ with $N1_\Lambda=0$. Every section $m$ of every $\Lambda$-module sheaf satisfies $Nm=(N1_\Lambda)m=0$; the same holds for its subquotients and hence cohomology sheaves. Extension by zero carries quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. Its exactness and [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology](c) give $\mathcal H^q(j_!K)=j_!\mathcal H^q(K)$, so $L=j_!K$ is bounded below. The exact inverse-image functors of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] likewise commute with homology and preserve this lower bound. All complexes to which we apply proper base change therefore lie in the stated bounded-below categories, and $\operatorname{For}L$ has torsion cohomology.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, label lemma-base-change-shriek, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Apply [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] to the cartesian square $(p,p',g,\overline g)$ and the bounded-below torsion abelian complex $\operatorname{For}L$ from step 2. Its exchange morphism is an isomorphism, with no condition on $g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients](1)--(3), forgetting coefficients identifies the module exchange map with that abelian exchange, and the final assertion of that node detects its invertibility. The abelian exchange is natural in $K$ by [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange]; the module exchange in clause (3) is the same mate construction with the module adjunctions. Its displayed composite of the natural unit, square isomorphism and counit is therefore natural as well. We obtain the natural isomorphism $g^{-1}Rp_*j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*\overline g^{-1}j_!K$ in the derived category of $\Lambda$-module sheaves. This is proper base change on small etale sites, without any change to pro-etale or structure-sheaf coefficients.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, label lemma-base-change-shriek, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Apply [cor-cbc-derived-extension-zero-base-change] to the open-immersion square $(j,j',\overline g,g')$ of step 1 and the finite commutative ring $\Lambda$. It supplies a natural isomorphism $\overline g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}j'_!g'^{-1}K$ for every $K\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Apply the functor $Rp'_*$ to this isomorphism. A functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse morphisms, so we obtain $Rp'_*\overline g^{-1}j_!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp'_*j'_!g'^{-1}K$.

source.place: Tag 0F7L, label lemma-base-change-shriek, first proof paragraph

proof.text: Compose the isomorphisms of steps 3 and 4. Substituting $Rf_!^c=Rp_*j_!$ and $Rf'_!^{c'}=Rp'_*j'_!$ from [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification] gives $g^{-1}Rf_!^cK\cong Rf'_!^{c'}g'^{-1}K$. Both factors are natural in $K$, so their composite is natural: for any morphism $a:K\to K_1$, compose the two commuting naturality squares along their common edge. The item fixes $c$ and its pullback $c'$; no independence of compactification or pasting assertion is needed for its conclusion.
